html:
Lekki Deep Sea Port is a deep water port in the Lagos Free Zone on the Lekki peninsula, east of Lagos, Nigeria. It began full commercial work in April 2023 and is the country's largest seaport and one of the biggest in West Africa.

For decades Nigeria's trade squeezed through the old ports of Apapa and Tin Can Island in central Lagos. Their channels are too shallow for the largest container ships, and trucks waiting to reach them clogged the city's roads for kilometres. Lekki was built on open coast where deep water lies close to shore.

The port was built by the China Harbour Engineering Company, which is also a shareholder alongside the Singapore based Tolaram group and the Nigerian Ports Authority. The Dangote Refinery stands nearby on the same peninsula. Plans call for further expansion as trade grows.
